page: Microsoft Azure F1ads_v7 is an entry-level virtual machine within Azure's compute-focused lineup, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by a dedicated single physical core and single vCPU from an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture provides 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a substantial 32 MB L3 cache slice, alongside instruction set support including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions), AES, and SHA-NI cryptography acceleration. It is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM profile.

Storage consists of an included 118 GB local NVMe SSD, providing high-speed scratch space directly attached to the host. No discrete GPU acceleration is included on this instance type. In benchmark testing, the high operating clock frequency and architecture of the AMD EPYC 9V45 yield top-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng as well as top-tier compression execution speeds, registering 38.66 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 16.95 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

Performance tradeoffs center on the single-core limitation. Aggregate multithreaded capacity and parallel throughput metrics—such as multi-core stress-ng, PassMark aggregate CPU evaluations, static web serving (2.63 GB/sec), and PassMark database operations—place in the lower percentiles relative to multi-core cloud instances. Large memory read bandwidth reaches 39.12 GB/sec uncached, while write bandwidth stabilizes at 31.44 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1ads_v7 offers an economical deployment model for dedicated compute resources that require sustained single-thread clock speed without the overhead of multi-core licensing or allocation costs. Appropriate workloads include lightweight batch processing, single-threaded compression utilities, automation agents, development environments, and small-footprint background workers.
description: Microsoft Azure F1ads_v7 is a compact compute-oriented instance powered by a single dedicated vCPU from a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM and 118 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system benefits from a large 32 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 vector support. In synthetic evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-threaded performance in stress-ng testing and single-core compression benchmarks, such as gzip and bzip3. However, overall multi-core processing, static web serving throughput, and database transaction scores remain bounded by its single-thread design. With no discrete GPU and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads prioritizing dedicated single-core compute over parallel execution. It is suited for lightweight automation agents, single-threaded processing tasks, development sandboxes, and low-concurrency microservices.
